s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic photosensitive eruption with systemic and cutaneous manifestations
salient_findings: Photosensitive eruption involving face, neck, trunk, and extremities
Poikiloderma on upper chest, anterolateral thighs, and extensor arms
Erythematous, flat-topped papules on extensor joints of hands
key_facts: Age of onset: 8 years
Duration of symptoms: 6 years
Previous treatments tried: systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, rituximab, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG)
Minimal improvement with previous treatments
Violaceous erythema on forehead and midface
Diffuse poikiloderma on upper chest, anterolateral thighs, and extensor arms
Erythematous, flat-topped papules on extensor joints of hands
Dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles on nailfold examination
Elevated serum IFN-β levels (8 pg/mL, normal ≤2 pg/mL)
Presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies
Radiographic evidence of myositis

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical examination revealed violaceous erythema, diffuse poikiloderma, and erythematous flat-topped papules, consistent with dermatomyositis. Elevated serum IFN-β levels and presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies also support this diagnosis.

shortlist.label: Lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including photosensitive eruption and systemic manifestations, are consistent with lupus erythematosus. However, the presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies is more specific to dermatomyositis.

shortlist.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlap of symptoms, including myositis and cutaneous manifestations, could suggest mixed connective tissue disease. However, the presence of specific autoantibodies and clinical findings point more towards dermatomyositis.

shortlist.label: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age and symptoms, including erythematous flat-topped papules on extensor joints, could suggest juvenile idiopathic arthritis. However, the presence of specific autoantibodies and clinical findings point more towards dermatomyositis or lupus erythematosus.

shortlist.label: Poikiloderma with neutropenia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including diffuse poikiloderma, could suggest poikiloderma with neutropenia. However, the presence of specific autoantibodies and clinical findings point more towards dermatomyositis or lupus erythematosus.

raw.rationale: The presence of violaceous erythema, diffuse poikiloderma, erythematous flat-topped papules, dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles, along with radiographic evidence of myositis and elevated serum IFN-β levels, are characteristic features of dermatomyositis. The presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies also supports this diagnosis, as they are commonly found in dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: While lupus can present with similar skin findings, the specific combination of features and the presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies are more suggestive of dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a combination of features from lupus, scleroderma, and rheumatoid arthritis, which are not all present in this case.

rejected.label: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis
rejected.why: The skin and nail findings, as well as the presence of myositis, are not typical of juvenile idiopathic arthritis.

rejected.label: Poikiloderma with neutropenia
rejected.why: While poikiloderma is present, the other features such as violaceous erythema, myositis, and specific autoantibodies are not characteristic of poikiloderma with neutropenia.
